frame.restated: An adversary with existing access to compromised Windows hosts is using remote execution or authentication mechanisms to pivot to additional hosts on the network.
frame.what_would_confirm: Remote service creation or SMB/PsExec/WinRM/RDP/SSH logons from a compromised host to other hosts, remote scheduled task or WMI execution, pass-the-hash/ticket authentication to new hosts, or service/process artifacts on destination hosts originating from the source host.
frame.what_would_refute: No remote logons or remote execution events originating from compromised hosts to other hosts, no new host-to-host authentication or service creation, and no evidence of credential reuse or remote session establishment beyond normal baseline.

verdict.rationale: 5 in-scope incident(s) of verified malicious findings (confidence >= medium): I03 T1021.002 (F01, F07, F11, F16, F18), I05 T1021.006 (F02, F12), I06 T1072 (F31), I08 T1570 (F23), I09 T1570 (F27)
verdict.rule: Confirmed if >=1 in-scope incident of verified malicious findings (confidence >= medium); Inconclusive if only suspicious incidents or coverage gaps; Refuted if full coverage and no malicious/suspicious finding

T1021.name: Remote Services
T1021.reason: Remote service use from scranton.dmevals.local (10.0.1.4) by pbeesly against nashua.dmevals.local: WinRM Invoke-Command to NASHUA followed by four PsExec64 executions with cleartext credentials, PSEXESVC service installs and ADMIN$ access on NASHUA.

T1021.001.name: Remote Desktop Protocol
T1021.001.reason: New: LogonType 2 interactive sessions for pbeesly on NASHUA at 03:11:40, 03:12:46, 03:13:49, 03:15:03, each paired with a PsExec network logon from 10.0.1.4 and PSEXESVC.exe/python.exe start.

T1021.002.name: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
T1021.002.reason: New: pbeesly LogonType 3 from 10.0.1.4 (SCRANTON) to NEWYORK at 03:04:04 followed by IPC$ share access, plus a further pbeesly network logon from 10.0.1.6 (NASHUA) at 03:14:20 — SMB access to the DC beyond the anchored NASHUA PsExec.

T1021.003.name: Distributed Component Object Model
T1021.003.reason: No DCOM artifacts: no LogonType 3 with svchost process name, no MMC20.Application/ShellWindows/ShellBrowserWindow script blocks; only a benign Invoke-CimMethod alias definition.

T1021.004.name: SSH
T1021.004.reason: No port 22 connections in sysmon or zeek, no sshd service installs, no ssh/plink script blocks.

T1021.005.name: VNC
T1021.005.reason: No port 5900 connections, no vnc/tvnserver binaries, services or script blocks.

T1021.006.name: Windows Remote Management
T1021.006.reason: Invoke-Command -ComputerName NASHUA executed by pbeesly on SCRANTON with matching powershell.exe outbound TCP 5985 connections from 10.0.1.4 to 10.0.1.6, immediately preceding the PsExec movement to the same host.

T1072.name: Software Deployment Tools
T1072.reason: Confirmed and extended: PsExec-deployed python.exe on NASHUA then deployed Rar.exe and sdelete64.exe into C:\Windows\Temp and executed them.

T1080.name: Taint Shared Content
T1080.reason: All share activity in the retrieved events is read-only or PsExec service staging, not tainting of shared content. 5145/5140 events touch only SYSVOL (read masks 0x100081/0x120089 on GPO files), IPC$ and ADMIN$; Zeek smb_files shows exclusively SMB::FILE_OPEN on \\NEWYORK.dmevals.local\sysvol with no write/rename/delete; Sysmon event.code 11 shows no UNC/network-path file creations; 7045 service ImagePaths are local (%SystemRoot%\PSEXESVC.exe, C:\Windows\System32\javamtsup.exe). The ADMIN$ writes of PSEXESVC.exe and Temp\python.exe by pbeesly from 10.0.1.4 to nashua are remote-execution staging (T1021.002/T1569.002), and the Invoke-Exfil script block writes to a WebDAV share for exfiltration - neither is T1080.

T1091.name: Replication Through Removable Media
T1091.reason: No removable-media activity exists in the data. All non-C: drive writes are fixed-disk operations: DFSRs.exe writing F:\System Volume Information\DFSR\Config\*.XML.TMP on newyork (14 events) and smss.exe creating D:\pagefile.sys on scranton. windows.other volume-health events identify C:, D: and \\?\Volume{d1b3f076-...} as \Device\HarddiskVolume* fixed disks; no USB/removable device or drive-insertion events were found, and the Sysinternals Volumeid.exe files were written to C:\Users\pbeesly\Downloads. The lateral movement that is present (PsExec64 from scranton to \\NASHUA launching C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe, then Rar.exe archiving and sdelete64 wiping) is SMB/network-based, not removable-media replication.

T1210.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
T1210.reason: NEWYORK (DC) received pbeesly network logons and IPC$ access from both compromised hosts (10.0.1.4 and 10.0.1.6); no successful remote code execution observed there.

T1534.name: Internal Spearphishing
T1534.reason: Internal spearphishing/lateral execution continued: PsExec with pbeesly's plaintext password launched python.exe on NASHUA four times, which then ran PowerShell, Rar and sdelete.

T1550.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material
T1550.reason: Cleartext pbeesly credentials reused by PsExec64.exe from SCRANTON against NASHUA (four invocations with -u dmevals\pbeesly -p ...).

T1550.002.name: Pass the Hash
T1550.002.reason: One NTLM (NtLmSsp, NTLM V2) type-3 logon for pbeesly on scranton from 172.18.39.2, consistent with the PsExec alternate-credential move; no credential-dumping precursor or anomalous LSASS access, so pass-the-hash itself is not confirmed.

T1550.003.name: Pass the Ticket
T1550.003.reason: Kerberos 4769 requests are normal TGT/service-ticket acquisitions from 10.0.1.4; no PreAuthType 0 logons and zero Rubeus/kirbi/asktgt script blocks.

T1563.name: Remote Service Session Hijacking
T1563.reason: No session hijacking artifacts: no tscon/mstsc/qwinsta/query session process creations, no Enter-PSSession/New-PSSession script blocks. The 120 PowerShell 4104 matches were built-in CimCmdlets module text containing 'Session'/'CimSession'. The only remote-interactive logon (scranton, 03:20:46Z, pbeesly from 172.18.39.2) is a fresh LogonType 10 session with rdpclip/explorer/LogonUI spawned by TermService. Actual lateral movement was PsExec (T1021.002), outside this family.

T1563.002.name: RDP Hijacking
T1563.002.reason: The single inbound 3389 connection (scranton, 172.18.39.2 -> 10.0.1.4, Initiated false) corresponds to a legitimate new RDP logon for pbeesly (LogonType 10, User32, TerminalSessionId 2, rdpclip.exe child of TermService). No tscon.exe execution, no session redirection, no mstsc/winrs/ssh command lines — no evidence of RDP session takeover.

T1570.name: Lateral Tool Transfer
T1570.reason: New: Rar.exe and sdelete64.exe written into C:\Windows\Temp on NASHUA by the attacker's python.exe and executed for archiving and anti-forensic deletion; Sysinternals suite downloaded to SCRANTON.

checks.purpose: VNC server installed as a service (remote-control backdoor)
Network logons that may accompany VNC authentication to a host
Scripted VNC setup or connections
Inbound VNC flows (port 5900) between hosts in the Zeek window
Stack successful logons by LogonType to see if type 3 (network) / 10 (RemoteInteractive) logons from remote hosts stand out against baseline, indicating WinRM/RDP pivots.
Rare LogonProcessName values (e.g. NtLmSsp, Kerberos, User32) reveal remote authentication mechanisms used to reach other hosts.
Explicit-credential logons (4648) show a process on one host authenticating with alternate credentials to another host, a lateral-movement indicator.

findings.title: PsExec over SMB ADMIN$ from SCRANTON to NASHUA with cleartext credentials, repeated 4x
findings.summary: On 2020-05-02 between 03:11:18 and 03:14:42 UTC, user DMEVALS\pbeesly on scranton.dmevals.local (10.0.1.4) launched C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\PsExec64.exe from a PowerShell parent four times, each time targeting \\NASHUA with the password supplied on the command line (-u dmevals\pbeesly -p Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by -i 2 C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe). On nashua.dmevals.local the PSEXESVC service was installed four times (7045) and 4648 explicit-credential logons were recorded with process C:\Windows\PSEXESVC.exe, and ADMIN$ (\\*\ADMIN$, Share Path \??\C:\windows) was accessed from source 10.0.1.4 by pbeesly. This is classic SMB/admin-share lateral movement with remote service creation and execution of a payload from C:\Windows\Temp.

PsExec64.exe was run four times from PowerShell on SCRANTON (03:11:18, 03:12:25, 03:13:28, 03:14:42) with pbeesly's cleartext password to launch C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe on NASHUA; afterwards sdelete64.exe was used to wipe the stager and the downloaded tooling.

findings.title: PowerShell remoting (WinRM) from SCRANTON to NASHUA to enumerate sessions
findings.summary: At 2020-05-01T23:09:23 (03:09:23 UTC) on scranton.dmevals.local, pbeesly ran Invoke-Command -ComputerName NASHUA to enumerate processes/sessions of the same user on the remote host. Sysmon recorded the matching outbound TCP connections from powershell.exe (PID 3852, 10.0.1.4) to 10.0.1.6 on port 5985 at 03:09:23-03:09:29, with the reciprocal inbound connections logged on nashua.dmevals.local. This WinRM reconnaissance immediately preceded the PsExec lateral movement to the same target.

findings.title: PsExec used from scranton to deploy and run C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe on nashua (lateral movement)
findings.summary: On 2020-05-02 between 03:11:18 and 03:15:03 UTC, user pbeesly on scranton.dmevals.local repeatedly launched C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\PsExec64.exe from powershell.exe with the command line "C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\PsExec64.exe" -accepteula \\NASHUA -u dmevals\pbeesly -p Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by -i 2 C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe (four executions: 03:11:18, 03:12:25, 03:13:28, 03:14:42). Each execution caused the PSEXESVC service to be installed on nashua.dmevals.local (event 7045, Service File Name %SystemRoot%\PSEXESVC.exe, LocalSystem, demand start) and PSEXESVC.exe to start under services.exe, which then spawned C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe as pbeesly (03:11:40, 03:12:46, 03:13:49, 03:15:03). The python.exe process wrote a BAM UserSettings registry value for its own path, confirming execution. This is abuse of a software-deployment/remote-execution tool to move laterally from a compromised host (scranton, where sdelete64.exe was used to wipe C:\programdata\victim\???cod.3aka3.scr and other files) to nashua, with credentials passed in cleartext on the command line. No SCCM/Intune/SMS deployment-agent activity was observed (C059 zero hits); the deployment-tool artifact here is PsExec.

findings.title: Attacker tooling on SCRANTON: sdclt/csc payload compilation, hostui.exe and sdelete cleanup
Lateral movement present in the data is PsExec over SMB (not removable media) from scranton to nashua
findings.summary: While hunting T1091 I found that the actual lateral movement in this window is network-based, not removable-media based: user pbeesly on scranton.dmevals.local repeatedly ran C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\PsExec64.exe with the cleartext credential -u dmevals\pbeesly -p Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by against \\NASHUA to launch C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe (03:11:18Z, 03:12:25Z, 03:13:28Z, 03:14:42Z). On nashua.dmevals.local, C:\Windows\PSEXESVC.exe was created by services.exe and spawned C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe as pbeesly, followed by C:\Windows\Temp\Rar.exe archiving working.zip with password -hpfGzq5yKw and sdelete64.exe wiping Rar.exe, working.zip and Draft.Zip. This is malicious lateral movement/execution, but it is T1021.002/T1570-style SMB service execution, not T1091 replication through removable media, so it does not substantiate the T1091 hypothesis.

findings.title: WinRM (port 5985) remote-service access from compromised SCRANTON to NASHUA under user pbeesly
findings.summary: On 2020-05-02 between 03:09:23 and 03:09:29 UTC, PowerShell (C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe) running as pbeesly on scranton.dmevals.local (10.0.1.4) made four outbound connections to 10.0.1.6 on port 5985 (WinRM). At 03:09:23.885 the same second, nashua.dmevals.local spawned wsmprovhost.exe -Embedding as pbeesly, i.e. the WinRM remote shell was established on the target. windows.security corroborates with Kerberos network logons (LogonType 3) for pbeesly on nashua.dmevals.local sourced from 10.0.1.4 at 23:10:23, 23:11:18, 23:12:25 and 23:13:28 local time. This is remote-service access to a second host, not normal System/SMB traffic (SMB to 10.0.0.4 was exclusively process 'System').

findings.title: Post-access interactive collection and RAR archiving on NASHUA via the remote shell
findings.summary: Immediately after the WinRM session opened, PowerShell script blocks on nashua.dmevals.local as pbeesly enumerate processes (Get-Process -IncludeUserName), then at 23:15:59 local time recursively collect documents, archives, password/login/admin/VPN-named files and images from the user profile and compress them with Compress-Archive, followed by '.\Rar.exe a -hpfGzq5yKw "$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\working.zip" "$env:APPDATA\working.zip"' from C:\Windows\Temp at 23:16:19 and 'exit'. This is hands-on-keyboard activity on the newly reached host, consistent with staging data after remote-service access.

findings.title: Steganographic PowerShell loader (monkey.png) on SCRANTON — origin of the lateral movement
findings.summary: On scranton.dmevals.local at 2020-05-01 22:58:45 local (2020-05-02T02:58:46Z) a PowerShell 4104 script block as pbeesly decodes a bitmap C:\Users\pbeesly\Downloads\monkey.png into a byte array and executes it with IEX — a known APT29 steganography loader. This is the compromised host from which the WinRM connections to NASHUA (10.0.1.6) later originated, so it is the source of the remote-service access rather than a benign administrative script.

incidents.rationale: F19 reports the only NTLM LogonType 3 for pbeesly on scranton (NtLmSsp, NTLM V2) from 172.18.39.2, temporally consistent with the PsExec activity, with no pass-the-hash evidence. Best fit is Pass the Hash (T1550.002) as the alternate-authentication-material hypothesis, kept suspicious/medium.

incidents.title: PsExec tool transfer from SCRANTON to NASHUA via ADMIN$ share (PSEXESVC.exe + python.exe dropped)
incidents.rationale: not grouped by the consolidation step

incidents.title: Tool transfer onto NASHUA: python.exe, Rar.exe and sdelete64.exe written to C:\Windows\Temp and executed
incidents.rationale: F27 describes the attacker-written python.exe on nashua writing Rar.exe and sdelete64.exe to C:\Windows\Temp, then spawning powershell/cmd to run Rar.exe and sdelete64.exe for archiving and anti-forensic cleanup. This is tool staging/transfer onto the victim host, best fit Lateral Tool Transfer (T1570).

incidents.title: Sysinternals suite downloaded to SCRANTON and accessChk.exe run for permission enumeration
incidents.rationale: F29 describes powershell.exe as pbeesly downloading SysinternalsSuite.zip to Downloads, extracting it, and running accesschk.exe from C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite at 03:04:34 before the PsExec movement. This is tool staging on the host, best fit Lateral Tool Transfer (T1570), kept suspicious/medium.

incidents.title: Steganographic PowerShell loader (monkey.png) on SCRANTON
incidents.rationale: F14 describes a PowerShell 4104 script block decoding monkey.png into a byte array and executing it with IEX on scranton. This is obfuscated payload execution on the source host, not lateral movement, so out-of-scope:T1027.

incidents.title: PowerShell Invoke-Exfil script on SCRANTON copies archive to remote WebDAV share
incidents.rationale: F25 describes a 4104 script block defining Invoke-Exfil that installs 7Zip4Powershell, compresses Downloads into OfficeSupplies.7z with password 'lolol', maps \\192.168.0.4\webdav with hardcoded credentials and Copy-Items the archive there. This is exfiltration over an alternate channel, not lateral movement, so out-of-scope:T1048.

incidents.title: Post-access collection and RAR archiving on NASHUA via the remote shell
incidents.rationale: F13 describes hands-on collection on nashua: process enumeration, recursive file collection from the user profile, Compress-Archive and Rar.exe archiving into working.zip. This is collection/archive staging, not lateral movement, so out-of-scope:T1560.
